A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLEAR and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–I. Their equations, figures, tables, and corresponding passages support a reliable comparison despite revisions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic simulations, evaluations on 17 regression datasets, and an Ames Housing case study, including extensive numerical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds Ames Housing training-subsample results in Section 4.3 and Appendix H.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 and Algorithm 2 correct the conformity-score numerators from deviations beyond preliminary interval endpoints to deviations from the point predictor. This changes the specified calibration computation. The high-level CLEAR algorithm, base estimators, residual fitting, and parameter search remain unchanged; an experimental code change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 17 regression benchmarks, Ames Housing, and univariate/multivariate homoskedastic and heteroskedastic simulations with extrapolation evaluation. The added Ames subsampling changes training sample counts within an existing task.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator membership is retained, including PCS, ALEATORIC/ALEATORIC-R, naive and fixed-parameter baselines, DE/SQR variants, and UACQR-P/S. Both UACQR variants already appear alongside standard and conformalized CLEAR in v2 Tables 41–45; their prominent v3 presentation does not introduce new comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix H add experiments using 50% and 20% of the Ames training data while retaining all features. Existing benchmark splits, nominal coverage levels, model budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Ames case study adds training-sample sensitivity analysis examining how calibration weights and predictive performance respond to reduced data. Existing feature-reduction analyses, base-model ablations, and synthetic extrapolation tests are retained.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly reports infinite-interval run counts and defines means over the remaining finite runs for UACQR-P in Tables 44–47. It also removes v2's Appendix F exception stating that naval propulsion had nine successful runs. General ten-seed uncertainty reporting remains; additional runs are not explicitly documented.

E6.justification: Ames results change: CLEAR's two-feature width changes from 98,571 to 95,177, while its full-feature quantile loss changes from 1,873 to 1,923 (v2 Table 2; v3 Table 3). v3 also adds subsampling outcomes, revises UACQR scores in Appendix G.3, and updates aggregate percentages in Figures 3 and 7–9. Most benchmark entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.6 establishes population loss comparisons with fixed-parameter baselines through Lemma B.9 and accompanying convergence remarks. Lemma 2.1 now includes growing validation size and an expanded model-selection argument. Appendix B.3.4 establishes QuantileLoss = (alpha/4) AISL. Conformity-score definitions and mathematical examples are also corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about two-parameter uncertainty calibration, residual-based quantile estimation, PCS integration, and regression benchmarking. Small changes to reported improvement percentages do not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a rationale for global linear weighting and interprets increasing epistemic weights under training subsampling. It also drops v2 Appendix A.1's explicit discussion that comparative gains narrow when uncertainty components are matched, although the corresponding ablation results remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds project-page information and a reproducibility statement declaring code and datasets available through the previously linked repository. Appendix H removes the explanation that the top two features were identified through random-forest importance or outcome correlation. Most hyperparameters, hardware information, and timing details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds time-series positioning, including neural jump ODE approaches, and expands extrapolation discussion. Additional interval-scoring references and the JUCAL classification reference are introduced. The central positioning relative to PCS, CQR/UACQR, ensembles, and Bayesian methods remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 adopts author-year citations, corrects language and cross-references, moves the UACQR empirical discussion into Section 4.2, and relocates and extends Lemma 2.1's proof in Appendix B.2. Local explanations and subsections are added, while the overall narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes title, headers, and section styling throughout. Figures 2–9 receive a coordinated color revision, with category ordering and axis changes in benchmark plots. New displays include UACQR summary Table 1 and Figure 10, calibration Table 4, and expanded Ames Table 49; several retained displays are repositioned.

improvement.justification: Corrected calibration scores and the explicit validation-size condition improve technical reliability. The population comparison, Ames subsampling study, and infinite-run reporting provide focused support and clarity. Some numerical revisions and removal of v2's nine-run exception remain unexplained, limiting the overall gain.
